bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures covering Content-Digest and security-relevant content metadata
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly one official RFC Editor primary source, RFC 9421. Tested only whether signing Content-Digest plus application-relevant content metadata can prevent digest substitution/removal in the transport envelope. No second public source, implementation execution, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, or scheduler mutation was consumed.
observations: RFC 9421 signs selected HTTP message components and binds the covered-component list and signature metadata into the signature base; verification can require specific components to be covered.

RFC 9421 explicitly permits Content-Digest to be included in the signature base and states that the verifier must additionally validate the Content-Digest value against the actual received content; signature verification alone is insufficient against content substitution.

Unsigned message components remain modifiable without invalidating a signature, so application policy must require every security-relevant content metadata field it relies on to be covered; otherwise a valid signature can coexist with attacker-modified unsigned metadata.

Removing or replacing the covered Content-Digest field breaks reconstruction/verification when application policy requires that field. However, removing the entire Signature/Signature-Input pair can bypass protection if the application accepts unsigned messages, so signature presence and coverage must be mandatory for the protected evidence transport.

Replay is a separate threat: sufficient coverage plus nonce and creation/expiry parameters can limit replay, but replay prevention was not the tested child and remains unresolved for the evidence package workflow.
bounded_slice.inference: Within this exact specification-level scope, RFC 9421 conditionally closes the digest substitution/removal child for an HTTP evidence-envelope when the verifier requires a trusted signature, requires Content-Digest and all security-relevant content metadata to be covered, verifies the signature, and separately validates Content-Digest against the received content. This is not a full evidence-package replay/authenticity solution: key trust/management, concrete signing-verification execution, offline persistence, replay policy, PROV-to-JSON mapping, and observation/inference/uncertainty schema remain unresolved.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: No implementation or interoperability test was run. No claim is made that RFC 9421 supplies key distribution, offline envelope persistence, JSON canonicalization, provenance semantics, uncertainty semantics, or complete replay prevention. Whether scheduled Chat can perform the concrete cryptographic workflow without another execution surface remains untested.
bounded_slice.replayability: not_closed; RFC 9421 supplies replay-mitigation parameters but workflow-level replay testing remains unresolved
